title: China has the APEC stage. But Japan may have the momentum
gist: Ahead of China hosting APEC (18-19 November 2026), Chatham House argues that while Beijing dominates economically, Japan is gaining momentum as the Indo-Pacific's trusted, results-oriented convener via a pragmatic FOIP update (digital corridor, $10bn POWERR Asia, ASEAN-Japan AI initiative), top trust rankings in ASEAN, and efforts to keep the US engaged. Expectations for APEC unity are low; attention shifts to a likely Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral on the Iran war.

insights.claim: Expectations for the November 2026 APEC summit in Beijing and the preceding ASEAN summit in the Philippines are low, with a display of unity or a collective action plan seen as remote because China will keep leveraging its chokeholds on the global economy.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Do not price multilateral breakthroughs from APEC; headline risk sits in bilateral sideline meetings instead.
insights.quote: The possibility of a display of unity, let alone a collective action plan, seems remote, especially as China will continue to leverage its chokeholds on the global economy.

insights.claim: A likely trilateral meeting between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the 2026 APEC summit is expected to focus on the Iran war and denuclearization.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: A US-China-Russia trilateral is a key event risk for oil prices and Iran-war-related energy premia.

insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Energy-importing Asian economies like Vietnam are levered to any Iran ceasefire; watch them as relief-trade beneficiaries.

insights.claim: Despite China's remarkable record of lifting people out of poverty, there is a trust deficit across the Indo-Pacific, where Beijing has become the undisputed regional hegemon.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Regional hedging against Beijing supports demand for non-Chinese partners in infrastructure, energy and tech.

insights.claim: China will remain an indispensable relationship for every Indo-Pacific country, but Japan may hold the key to a collaborative path that lets the region keep its upward economic trajectory.

themes.theme: Japan's pragmatic FOIP 2.0: cables, energy, AI

insights.claim: Japan's Free and Open Indo-Pacific (FOIP) strategy originally championed a rules-based order and became the foundation for US and EU Indo-Pacific strategies, but its weakness was reluctance by South and Southeast Asian nations and weakening global commitment to rules-based order.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Values-based framing underdelivered in the Global South; practical deliverables are now the competitive currency.

insights.claim: In a May 2026 speech at Vietnam National University, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi set out a results-oriented FOIP update including AI-age economic infrastructure such as undersea cables and satellite communications forming a 'FOIP digital corridor'.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Watch Japanese subsea cable, satellite and telecom infrastructure contractors for Southeast Asia project flow.
insights.quote: initiatives to build economic infrastructure ‘for the age of AI’, such as underwater sea cables and satellite communications, creating a ‘FOIP digital corridor’.

insights.claim: Japan is expanding its $10 billion Partnership on Wide Energy and Resource Resilience Asia (POWERR Asia) and collaborating with the World Bank to advance regional energy resilience.

insights.so_what: A $10bn-plus, World Bank-linked energy-resilience pipeline is a funding source for Asian energy infrastructure.

insights.claim: Japan is boosting regional AI cooperation through an ASEAN-Japan Co-Creation Initiative for AI as part of its updated FOIP strategy.
insights.speaker: Chatham House

themes.theme: Japan as most-trusted convener, not leader

insights.claim: In the latest State of Southeast Asia survey, Japan was ranked the most trusted major power by respondents across the 10 ASEAN nations for the eighth consecutive year, with nearly 66 per cent viewing it as a responsible stakeholder.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Durable soft-power advantage favours Japanese firms in politically sensitive ASEAN infrastructure deals.
insights.quote: Japan is ranked the most trusted major power by respondents in the 10 ASEAN nations for the eighth consecutive year.

insights.claim: Japan-South Korea relations have improved as pragmatism prevailed over tensions, driven by shared economic concerns, increasing unpredictability of US policy, and common threats like North Korea.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: US unpredictability is pushing US allies toward closer bilateral coordination, a supportive backdrop for Japan-Korea supply-chain ties.
insights.locator: And it has shown an ability

insights.claim: Japan's inability to match China's economic heft or US technological and financial firepower, plus domestic fiscal constraints, may be an advantage, positioning it as a convener that delivers tangible results without demanding allegiance.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Middle-power 'no strings' partnership can win share in Global South deals versus allegiance-seeking great powers.
insights.quote: Japan is positioning itself not as a regional leader, but as the convener the Indo-Pacific increasingly needs.

themes.theme: Keeping the US engaged in Asian trade

insights.claim: There is growing discontent in the Indo-Pacific over economic damage from US foreign policy decisions, from tariffs to the war with Iran, while Japan keeps promoting frameworks to restore the US as a trusted economic power.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: US tariffs and the Iran war are eroding US economic standing in Asia; Japan acts as the bridge.

insights.claim: US accession to a multilateral trade framework such as the CPTPP is highly unlikely even after a new Democratic-controlled Congress is sworn in.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Do not expect a US return to Asian multilateral trade deals regardless of the Democratic Congress; tariff regime risk persists.

insights.so_what: Despite friction, Indo-Pacific economic-security alignment still anchors on US tech and capital.
